summary: Assigns a value for EdDSA public keys in the IANA registry of IPSECKEY resource record parameters. This lets such keys be published in the DNS for IPsec use.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9373 assigns an algorithm value for EdDSA public keys in DNS IPSECKEY records. The value lets an IPSECKEY record identify the key format using the definition in RFC 8080.

questions: how to publish eddsa keys for ipsec in dns
what is the eddsa ipseckey algorithm value
how are eddsa keys stored in ipseckey records
subtitle: An IPSECKEY registry value for EdDSA public keys stored in DNS.

tldr.problem: IPSECKEY records need an assigned algorithm value so their algorithm field can identify an EdDSA public key format.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns value 4 to EdDSA keys and points to RFC 8080 for the public-key format.
tldr.outcome: DNS IPSECKEY records can identify EdDSA public keys for IPsec use through the updated IANA registry entry.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 9373's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC assigns an IPSECKEY registry value for EdDSA public keys.

sections.title: Adding EdDSA to IPSECKEY
sections.content:
IPSECKEY is a DNS resource record used to store public keys for IPsec systems. Its algorithm type field uses a registry to identify permitted public-key formats.

This RFC adds support for EdDSA public keys in the format defined by RFC 8080 and updates the registry information for IPSECKEY algorithm types.
sections.plainLanguage: An IPSECKEY record stores a public key that IPsec systems can use. This RFC adds a registry value that identifies an EdDSA key.

sections.title: The EdDSA Algorithm Value
sections.content:
When an IPSECKEY resource record contains an EdDSA public key, the algorithm field uses value 4. The key itself is formatted as specified in section 3 of RFC 8080.

The RFC also adds a Format Description field to the algorithm registry and updates existing descriptions to identify the entries as public-key formats.
sections.plainLanguage: The number 4 tells a reader that the IPSECKEY data contains an EdDSA public key. The referenced specification defines how to encode that key.

sections.title: Registry Updates and Security
sections.content:
IANA added the EdDSA Public Key entry with value 4 and a reference to RFC 8080. The registry also gained a Format Description field, and existing descriptions were clarified to say when they identify public keys.

The RFC says the security considerations of RFC 4025 apply and that this registry update introduces no new security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry now lists EdDSA as an allowed IPSECKEY key format. The RFC relies on the existing IPSECKEY security guidance.
